question.problem: What is the domain in the $xy$-plane of the elliptic cylinder $(x+3)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{25}=1?$
question.worked_solution:
The full expression describing all points on our elliptic cylinder is

$$
(x+3)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{25}=1,\,z=k
$$

where $k\in R$ can vary arbitrarily. 

The domain of any cylinder in the $xy$-plane is its base curve. Hence, in this case, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:(x+3)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{25}=1\}
$$

which can be written as

$$
\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:\frac{(x+3)^{2}}{{1}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{5}^{2}}=1\}.
$$

This is an ellipse centered at $(-3,0)$ with semi-axes of lengths $1$ and $5.$
